description: if true then 1 else "a" end: Ty.joinTy has no *structural* case for (Int, an instance of String), but this is exactly the situation Ty.union exists for -- an explicit claim of union(Int, an instance of String) on the if' node is already expressible in the current grammar (see Ty.union's own docstring, "inert on the checker path" -- meant to be *claimed*, not inferred). No language gap; a rebuilt `if'` just needs a claim-fallback the same way `send`/`vcall` already have one.
